title: Pectin-based emulsion gels: Formation mechanisms, multiscale characterization, influencing factors and applications

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Pectin-based emulsion gels: Formation mechanisms, multiscale characterization, influencing factors and applications》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · p0025】Although many research articles have investigated pectin-based emulsion gels(Qi et al., 2024; Zhang, Zheng, et al., 2022; W. Y. Zhang et al., 2026), and several reviews have covered pectin hydrogels (Ishwarya et al., 2022; Nurul Saadah Said et al., 2023), pectin emulsification (Jia et al., 2024; Ngouemazong et al., 2012; Niu, Hou, et al., 2024), and food-grade emulsion gels (Lin et al., 2020; Lu et al., 2019), systematic attention devoted specifically to pectin-based emulsion gels remains comparatively limited. Relative to previous reviews that focus on pectin hydrogels, pectin emulsification or emulsion gels as a general class, the present work is devoted specifically to pectin-based emulsion gels. It integrates interfacial emulsification with multi-force gelation, treats the oil phase as an active network modulator, and examines unresolved RG-I/HG contributions under realistic oil fractions (Table 1).

【Introduction · p0030】The present review is organised around four themes: (1) preparation and formation mechanisms, including homogenization–interface coupling and multi-force gelation under realistic oil fractions, pH and protein co-solutes; (2) multiscale characterization linking texture, interfacial and bulk rheology, microstructure, and storage stability to process control; (3) structure–environment–property relationships, with emphasis on DM, RG-I architecture and pure versus composite systems; and (4) applications in food structuring, bioactive delivery, coatings and 3D printing, together with translational constraints of evidence quality and cost. The aim is to support more predictive design of pectin-based emulsion gels for food and related soft-matter uses.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Pectin-based emulsion gels: Formation mechanisms, multiscale characterization, influencing factors and applications》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Preparation method and formation mechanism of pectin-based emulsion gels · p0035】Pectin-based emulsion gels consist of oil droplets entrapped within a three-dimensional network (Fig. 2). Preparation generally follows two steps: (i) homogenization of a pectin dispersion with an oil phase by high-speed shear homogenization (HSSH), ultrasound homogenization (UH), high-pressure homogenization (HPH) or microfluidization homogenization (MH), and (ii) gelation of the continuous phase by acid, ionic (e.g., Ca2+, Mg2+, Zn2+), or enzymatic. Most studies use emulsion-first then gelation (Lin et al., 2020); pre-forming a hydrogel and then incorporating oil remains rare (X. Zhang et al., 2021). This section reviews emulsification, gelation mechanisms and the distinction between pure pectin and pectin–protein composite systems at the level of interfacial assembly.

【Molecular simulation approaches · p0250】Although direct molecular-dynamics studies of intact pectin emulsion gels remain scarce, the transferable insights already obtained from related polysaccharide systems point to several clear research priorities. Future simulations should move beyond single-component or simplified interfaces and explicitly incorporate realistic oil-volume fractions, mixed HG/RG-I architectures, residual protein moieties and physiologically relevant ionic conditions. Multi-scale approaches that couple all-atom descriptions of the interfacial film with coarse-grained representations of the continuous-phase network would allow the simultaneous capture of local chain orientation, side-chain entanglement and long-range droplet–matrix interactions. Equally important is the systematic mapping of free-energy barriers to coalescence and film rupture as functions of degree of methoxylation, RG-I branching density and calcium concentration. When such trajectories are quantitatively linked to experimental dilatational moduli, Cryo-SEM morphology and bulk gel strength, molecular simulation will evolve from a retrospective illustration into a predictive design tool capable of guiding the rational engineering of pectin-based emulsion gels for food, delivery and 3D-printing applications.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Pectin-based emulsion gels: Formation mechanisms, multiscale characterization, influencing factors and applications》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusion and prospects · p0425】Pectin-based emulsion gels are soft-matter systems in which functional properties emerge from the coupled processes of emulsification and gelation. Preparation typically involves homogenization (HSSH, UH, HPH or MH) followed by acid-, ion- or enzyme-induced gelation of the continuous phase.Performance is evaluated through texture, bulk and interfacial rheology, microstructure, and stability under thermal, mechanical, freeze–thaw, gastrointestinal and long-term storage stresses. These measurements together link interfacial adsorption and network formation to macroscopic performance.

【Conclusion and prospects · p0430】System behaviour depends on both pectin fine structure and the formulation environment. Molecular weight, degree and pattern of methoxylation, RG-I branching, and residual protein or feruloyl groups set the capacity for interfacial adsorption and network building; homogenization energy, oil-volume fraction, pH, ionic strength and protein co-solutes determine how much of that capacity is expressed. Classical, oil-free hydrogel models—centred on DM and simple acid or egg-box gelation—only partly explain emulsion gels. Above moderate oil fractions, droplets sterically disrupt long-range ionic bridges, while RG-I side chains can serve as interfacial anchors and entanglement sites—roles that HG-centric schemes largely overlook. Most studies still change one variable at a time in simplified systems, so transferable structure–interface–gel relationships under realistic food conditions remain limited.
